data.headline: Small-cap futures positioning diverges as SOFR edges down
data.summary: The November 3 E-mini Russell 2000 report showed a larger asset-manager net long and a larger leveraged-fund net short. November 9 SOFR was 3.88%, a basis point below November 6.

bull.text: The asset-manager net long rose from 19,602 to 23,623 contracts. The November 9 decline in SOFR can modestly ease costs for borrowers with floating-rate debt when their reset dates and credit terms allow.

bear.text: Leveraged funds increased their net short from 48,081 to 55,080 contracts between October 27 and November 3.

watch.text: Open interest fell from 458,959 to 449,399 contracts as the two categories diverged. Watch the next weekly report for whether both category moves persist.

limitations: SOFR measures overnight secured funding. Company borrowing rates also reflect credit spreads, reset dates and contract terms.
The CFTC observations are weekly futures positions as of November 3. ETF flows and investor intent require separate evidence.
